text: In the grammar of time, tense locates an event relative to a reference point such as the moment of utterance, whereas ___ characterizes the internal temporal structure of an event — whether it is completed (perfective), ongoing (imperfective), or habitual.
explanation: The book distinguishes tense (where an event is located in time) from aspect (how the event is shaped in time — perfective/completed versus imperfective/ongoing, habitual, and so on). The intended word is 'aspect'; it is precisely the category the passage contrasts with tense, so answering 'tense' would collapse the very distinction being drawn.
